newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end two pct down with futures, lira.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end two pct down with futures, lira.

text.p: Italian shares closed nearly two percent lower on Friday with the March bourse index future losing over 400 basis points as the lira dropped to below 1,000 per mark and bond futures fell over 200 basis points on EMU worries and a lower Wall Street, traders said.
"There are sell orders all over the place with worries about a delay of monetary union, although denied, sending Btps and the lira down," one trader said.
But prices closed above the session lows with the all-share Mibtel index down 1.54 pct at 11,745 after a low at 11,664 and the Mib30 blue chip index off 1.92 pct at 17,386.

A nervous market began weaker, continuing the technical correction begun mid-week. A brief collapse in state controlled energy group ENI's share price early on, suspended limit down, took the Mibtel index down to its session low before the stock recovered. ENI closed 1.98 percent down at 8,345 lire.
Wall Street got off to an easier start despite market friendly revised U.S. fourth quarter GDP data.

Telecoms were again under pressure on worries about lira weakness with dealers seeing profit-taking by foreign investors. "Foreign buyers are preferring to take their profits now before a depreciating lira eats into their gains," one trader said.
Telecoms holding Stet lost 3.53 percent to 7,250, mobile phone operator TIM shed 3.68 percent to 4,425 and Telecom Italia lost 1.73 percent to 3,970.

Fiat stock firmed against the trend on talk of good February car sales and with foreign auto stocks performing well. Fiat ended 2.55 percent higher at 5,220 while Agnelli family holding group IFIL gained 1.92 percent to 5,050.
Banks were generally weak, but Banco Ambrosiano Veneto put on 3.74 percent to 4,300 lire.
Traded volume was seen up on Thursday at around 1.14 trillion lire against 966 billion lire.
